field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: There were only a few boats fishing today and there was not much to report. The anglers caught some crabs and rock fish. The one angler looking for sea bass ran into bumpy conditions up the coast. There was one boat who ran up the coast after the wind died and they ended up with a 46 pound sea bass. The swell is still here but the wind has dropped. I hope tomorrow is a better day like N.O.A.A. says.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast November 21, 2026 Salmon fishing remains steady as anglers wait for the big rise Scott Manning of Healdsburg with a nice Smith River king landed earlier this week. Photo courtesy of Mike Coopman/ Mike Coopman’s Guide Service Well, the big storms didn’t quite materialize as planned, but they delivered just enough rain to get salmon anglers on the water. The storm door is definitely cracked open, but so far, we’ve seen only a parade of modest systems — just enough rain to bump flows, but nowhere near enough to produce the full-blown rises anglers hope for this time of year. It’s been a few storms here and there, keeping rivers barely high enough to remain open and allowing salmon to trickle upriver rather than charge in by the bunches. Despite the lack of a true gully-washer, these smaller rises have created some pretty good fishing windows. The brief bumps in flows have produced some solid scores for both boat and bank anglers who have been able to time their outings around the pulses of water. Fish continue to move with each rise, but how much longer this pattern will hold remains to be seen. Looking ahead to next week, the forecast is shaping up much the same:

field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: This Friday, November 20th there is a decent window for getting out there for some fishing. The Lingcod have been biting really well up to the time when the ocean conditions went really bad. So if you have time to get out there with us this will be the time. Give our office a call.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
